1.falsification: If the isolated alignment correction does not exceed baseline trial 0 HR@10=0.395, its proposed validation benefit is unsupported. If no pooling candidate exceeds the corrected control, recency pooling is unsupported under the frozen training and evaluation conditions. Execution failures are implementation failures, not scientific falsification; small score differences remain uncertain without replication.
1.hypothesis: Selecting the latest valid causal state will improve candidate ranking by correcting the right-alignment mismatch. Pooling a small number of recent valid states may further improve ranking by smoothing noisy recent preferences. All candidates start from untouched trial 0 and change only candidate readout inside NextItNetModel in model.py; preserve imports, training forward, encoding, both classes' remaining behavior and all eight numeric hyperparameters. Define h_last as the final nonpadding state and P(k,tau) as the normalized weighted mean of the last min(k, valid_length) nonpadding states, with weights exp(-age/tau), age zero for the latest state; tau=uniform means equal weights. Readout R=alpha*h_last+(1-alpha)*P. Empty histories produce a zero vector. Preserve the evaluator's existing candidate-score shape. Slot 1 isolates correctness; slots 2-10 are readout architecture comparisons against that corrected control. The controller runs the frozen BPR/Adam schedule and retains candidates only for strictly higher validation HR@10; ties and regressions restore the incumbent.
observables: Completed trial ID, execution status and validation HR@10 for every executed slot.
Slot 1 HR@10 minus untouched baseline trial 0 HR@10=0.395, isolating alignment correction.
Each pooling candidate's HR@10 minus slot 1 HR@10, separating pooling effects from the correctness fix.
Controller keep/discard outcome against the incumbent and any reported failure details.
Dependence of ranking quality on pooling window, recency weighting and latest-state mixture; no hidden-test evidence.
